mechanism: Gaussian mode-basis rotation (beam-splitter conjugation of a native CD) fusing two commuting Z_j-conditioned linear terms

rule.name: fused_dual_mode_conditional_displacement_by_balanced_bs
rule.idea: Two commuting qubit-conditioned linear mode terms exp(-i th Z_j x_j) exp(-i th' Z_j x_m), with x = a+a^+ and m the grid-neighbour partner mode of qubit j's home mode j, fuse into a single native CD on the home mode conjugated by a beam-splitter pair. Let G = a^+ b - b^+ a with a = mode j, b = mode m; V = e^{-sG} with s = atan2(th', th) rotates a into (th a + th' b)/sqrt(th^2+th'^2). Conjugating the native CD_j(beta) = exp(Z_j(beta a^+ - beta* a)) by V with beta = -i*sqrt(th^2+th'^2) gives exactly exp(-i Z_j(th x_j + th' x_m)), i.e. the product of the two target exponentials, with V realized as BS(2s, +-pi/2) in ISA form. This replaces the router's SWAP-in/CD/SWAP-out pattern for the off-home-mode term with a single beam-splitter pair and no ancilla, saving two-op gates and the associated R/SWAP overhead. The rewrite only fires if every op between the two CD terms commutes with both Z_j x_j and Z_j x_m (disjoint wires, or is the Z_j x_j term itself), and only if mode m is the fixed grid neighbour of mode j (0-4,1-5,2-6,3-7).
